primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors are ovarian sex cord-stromal neoplasms that recapitulate testicular-type differentiation. The Leydig-cell component can produce testosterone, causing rapid virilization, hirsutism, deepening of the voice, and menstrual disturbance. DICER1 pathogenic variants are strongly associated with many moderately and poorly differentiated tumors.
vignette: A 23-year-old woman presents with 7 months of secondary amenorrhea, rapidly progressive facial hair growth, acne, and deepening of her voice. Examination shows temporal hair recession and clitoromegaly. Serum testosterone is markedly elevated, but dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate is within the reference range. Pelvic ultrasonography shows a unilateral solid ovarian mass. The mass is resected.
lead: Which of the following microscopic findings would most strongly support the suspected diagnosis?
correct: Tubules and cords resembling Sertoli-cell structures admixed with clusters of steroid-producing Leydig-type cells
distractors: Call-Exner bodies composed of small follicles containing eosinophilic material and nuclei with longitudinal grooves
Sheets of large polygonal cells with clear cytoplasm and central nuclei separated by fibrous septa containing lymphocytes
Papillary structures containing fibrovascular cores with concentric calcified psammoma bodies
Mature tissues derived from multiple germ layers, including skin adnexa, cartilage, and respiratory-type epithelium
distractor_notes: Call-Exner bodies and coffee-bean nuclear grooves characterize granulosa cell tumor, another sex cord-stromal tumor that more often produces estrogen.
Clear cells in sheets with fibrous septa and lymphocytes describe dysgerminoma, an ovarian germ-cell tumor rather than an androgen-producing sex cord-stromal tumor.
Papillary architecture with psammoma bodies is typical of serous ovarian neoplasia and does not explain the virilizing endocrine pattern.
Mature derivatives of several germ layers characterize mature cystic teratoma and are not the characteristic Sertoli-Leydig architecture.
key_expl: Rapid virilization, markedly elevated testosterone with normal DHEA-S, and a unilateral ovarian mass indicate an androgen-producing ovarian tumor. Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor is a sex cord-stromal neoplasm with testicular-type differentiation; histology can show Sertoli-like tubules or cords with Leydig-type stromal cells. The alternative patterns correspond to granulosa cell tumor, dysgerminoma, serous neoplasia, and mature teratoma.
objective: Recognize ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor as a virilizing sex cord-stromal neoplasm and identify its characteristic Sertoli- and Leydig-type differentiation.
